chunks: From him (Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Umari), from al-Nadr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked:
About a village in which there is a mill, date palms, a garden, crops, and a date-pit (storage), and its produce was purchased. He said, 'There is no objection.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no objection/It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to engage in sharecropping where the landlord buys the produce from a village with mixed agricultural assets?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates a specific form of Muzara'ah where the landlord purchases the produce (Ghalla) rather than sharing the crop itself, provided the village possesses essential agricultural infrastructure like a mill, palms, and gardens. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding agricultural contracts, distinguishing between sharecropping and purchase agreements based on the presence of tangible assets and the nature of the transaction. It underscores the practical application of contract law in early Islamic society, ensuring that such arrangements do not fall into the category of prohibited uncertainty (Gharar).
